newsitem.title: BELARUS: Lukashenko "very busy", may not go to peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Lukashenko "very busy", may not go to peace talks.

text.p: Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko was "very busy" on Wednesday and might not find time to travel to Russia for peace talks with his opponents to defuse the republic's political crisis, an aide told Reuters.

"The president is very busy. He has a very tight schedule. I do not know if he will find a window in his schedule to go to Smolensk," Mikhail Podgainy, head of Lukashenko's information department, said by telephone.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin earlier spoke by telephone to Lukashenko, seeking to persuade him to compromise with his foes over plans for a referendum to increase his powers.

The talks in the western Russian city of Smolensk are set to involve the speakers of the two Russian chambers of parliament and the speaker of the Belarussian parliament, Semyon Sharetsky, who has accused Lukashenko of trying to impose a dictatorship.

Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is also expected to attend. Russia and Belarus formed a two-state "community" last April and the former Soviet republic is heavily dependent on its huge neighbour economically.
